# OffsetDateTime

A date and time together with the offset from UTC they are stated in.

```rux
pub struct OffsetDateTime {
    pub dateTime: DateTime;
    pub offset: UtcOffset;
}
```

[`DateTime`](/docs/api/time/date-time) deliberately carries no offset, since what offset a bare date and time is in is usually the caller's
knowledge rather than the value's. This is the pairing for when it is not: an instant written down for
interchange, where the offset is part of what was recorded and losing it changes the meaning.
`Copy`, and exactly as wide as its two halves.


The local date and time `dateTime` paired with the offset it is stated in.
Cannot fail: both halves are already valid, and no combination of a valid date-time and a valid offset is
invalid. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

## Implements Display

`OffsetDateTime` conforms to `Display`.

<h3 id="write-display"><code>WriteDisplay</code></h3>

```rux
pub func WriteDisplay(
    self: &OffsetDateTime,
    writer: &var TextWriter,
    spec: FormatSpec
) -> ! FormatError
```

Writes the moment as RFC 3339: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS[.fraction]` followed by `Z` or a signed `HH:MM`.
This is the type that can produce RFC 3339, because it is the one that carries an offset. The offset is
written as it is held rather than normalized to UTC: what was recorded includes where, and shifting it away
would discard that.
Reports whatever the writer reported, `UnsupportedRequest` for a style other than `iso8601` or `rfc3339`,
and `UnsupportedRequest` for a precision past nine.

| Name     | Type              | Description                    |
| -------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `writer` | `&var TextWriter` | the destination                |
| `spec`   | `FormatSpec`      | what the placeholder asked for |

**Returns**: success when the whole moment was accepted

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Time/Src/CalendarText.rux#L300)

## Related

<h3 id="parse-rfc3339"><code>ParseRfc3339</code></h3>

```rux
pub func ParseRfc3339(text: char8[..]) -> OffsetDateTime ! TimeParseError
```

Reads `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS[.fraction](Z|+HH:MM|-HH:MM)`.
The offset is required, which is what RFC 3339 requires and what makes the result a moment rather than a local
reading. Second 60 folds to the last nanosecond of second 59, as this package's leap-second policy states;
formatting never produces second 60, so the fold is one-way and the round trip is clean for every ordinary
moment.
The failures the date, time and offset readers report, plus `InvalidSyntax` for text after the offset. Each
carries the byte offset where it was found.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Time/Src/CalendarParse.rux#L280)

**Parameters**

| Name   | Type        | Description      |
| ------ | ----------- | ---------------- |
| `text` | `char8[..]` | the text to read |

**Returns**: the moment with the offset it was stated in, or why the text is not one
